timeline: Ch1: Iris Kane reviews the names of the sixty-three people killed in the Kessler Line tunnel collapse before opening her appointment letter.
Ch1: Iris discovers she has been appointed lead technical investigator for the Kessler Line Inquiry and must submit findings through the commission secretariat for approval.
Ch1: Iris notices that the terms of reference repeatedly frame the official cause as seismic microfracture compounded by dispatch error rather than allowing that premise to be questioned.
Ch1: Iris identifies subclause 4.3 as a barrier preventing review of procurement, vendors, contracts, policy decisions, and other matters classified as administrative discretion.
Ch1: Iris marks the phrase "administrative discretion," scans the appointment letter page by page, and uses her scanner's recurring blue-stripe defect to help detect later substitutions.
Ch1: Iris leaves the appointment acceptance block unsigned and turns to a second packet labeled Initial Forensic Archive.

knows: The Kessler Line collapse killed sixty-three passengers and employees.
The official cause is stated as seismic microfracture compounded by dispatch error.
Her appointment requires findings to pass through the commission secretariat for approval before circulation.
Subclause 4.3 excludes policy, procurement, vendor selection, contract authorization, and administrative discretion from review.
The delivered envelope bears a pressure mark indicating that a staple was removed before it reached her.
Iris Kane.relationship_other: Newly appointed lead technical investigator for the Kessler Line Inquiry, but distrustful of the commission's restrictive mandate.
Iris Kane.mood: Controlled, meticulous, skeptical, and alert to institutional manipulation.

facts_established: The Kessler Line eastbound tunnel collapsed during evening service.
Sixty-three passengers and employees died in the collapse.
Iris Kane has been appointed lead technical investigator to the Kessler Line Inquiry, effective immediately.
The inquiry's official stated cause is "Seismic microfracture compounded by dispatch error."
The terms of reference require Iris to submit findings for approval before circulation.
The inquiry remit includes reconstructing the mechanical failure sequence, assessing dispatch decisions, and recommending revisions to emergency operating procedure.
Subclause 4.3 prohibits review of policy-level determinations, procurement strategy, vendor selection, contract authorization, and administrative discretion.
The appointment envelope was hand-delivered without a courier signature or receipt.
A pressure mark on the envelope indicates that a staple had been removed before delivery.
Iris's document scanner adds a faint blue stripe to every seventh page, which she uses to make document substitutions easier to detect.
Iris has not signed the appointment acceptance block.
A second packet is labeled Initial Forensic Archive.
spice_progression: No romantic or sexual progression; the chapter establishes investigative tension and institutional distrust.
phrases_used: The body count arrived before the terms of reference.
Once was a description. Twice was emphasis. Three times was architecture.
The dead had occupations, addresses, and next-of-kin contacts. The terms of reference had subclauses.
an insulated wall around every decision made before engineering became physical
Acceptance of an appointment was not acceptance of its premise.
